structural.note: True duplicate: 'sticky rice' and 'glutinous rice' are the same ingredient and carry identical aliases (sweet rice, mochi rice, mochigome, thai sticky rice, khao niaow). glutinous-rice has the richer alias set (+black sticky rice) and the more canonical name, so it is the survivor. No item parents to or swaps 'sticky', so the merge dangles nothing.

Item is named 'wheat bran' and parented to 'bran', but its id is the bare, misleading 'wheat'. No item references the id 'wheat' as a parent/swap, so re-id is safe; gives it an id that matches the thing it is and removes the trap of a generic 'wheat' id pointing at bran.

cleanups.note: 'wheats' is a bare plural of generic 'wheat'. There is no generic wheat-grain item, so a 'wheat'/'wheats' query would mis-resolve to wheat BRAN. Over-broad alias on a specific (bran) item -> remove. (Targets the re-id'd id; reid runs in the structural pass first.)

Over-broad alias on the generic 'rice' base. A dedicated child 'rice-white' (name 'rice white') already covers white rice; carrying 'white rice' on the parent makes a 'white rice' query resolve to generic rice instead of the specific item.

Over-broad alias on the generic 'rice' base. 'long-grain rice' is a specific type; pinning it as an exact alias of generic rice short-circuits resolution to dedicated long-grain items (brown-rice/carolina-gold-rice carry the long-grain aliases). Generic 'rice' should stay generic.

'congee' is its own child item of 'porridge'. The alias on the parent shadows the dedicated child, so a 'congee' query competes between parent and child. Remove from parent; the congee item owns the name.
'rice porridge' is shared with 'congee'. Congee IS rice porridge; cream-of-rice is a ground-rice hot cereal (farina-style), not porridge. Keep 'rice porridge' on congee, remove the leaked alias here.

'rye grain' is shared with 'rye' (name 'rye groats'), the more generic rye entry that should own the bare 'rye grain' term. rye-berries keeps its specific aliases (whole rye kernels). Removes the duplicate alias collision.

'bajra' specifically denotes pearl millet, not generic millet, and is already (correctly) an alias of 'pearl-millet'. Carrying it on the generic 'millet' base is an over-broad leak; remove so 'bajra' resolves to pearl-millet.
